## What is GitHub Pages

- GitHub Pages publishes a repository as a free website
- No traditional server is needed
- The website can use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files
- The address is `username.github.io/repository-name`

## GitHub Pages Example

- Repository: [BusMgmtBenchmarks](https://github.com/calvinw/BusMgmtBenchmarks)
- Published website: [FIT Retail Index](https://calvinw.github.io/BusMgmtBenchmarks/)
- The repository contains the files
- GitHub Pages turns the files into a website

## The `index.html` File

- `index.html` is the main page of the website
- GitHub Pages looks for this file when the website opens
- Editing `index.html` changes the published page
- Changes appear after they are committed to the publishing branch

## Set Up GitHub Pages

1. Open the repository and select **Settings**
2. Select **Pages** under **Code and automation**
3. Under **Build and deployment**, choose **Deploy from a branch**
4. Select the `main` branch and the `/ (root)` folder
5. Click **Save**

## Watch the Deployment Progress

- Open the repository's **Actions** tab
- Watch the GitHub Pages deployment progress
- A yellow circle means the deployment is still running
- A green check mark means the deployment is complete
- Open the deployment to see more details

## Add the Website to the Repository

1. Open the repository's main page
2. Select the gear icon next to **About**
3. Enter the GitHub Pages address in the **Website** field
4. Save the changes

The website link now appears on the repository's main page.
